newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Icatu denies being asked to run Bamerindus.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Icatu denies being asked to run Bamerindus.

text.p: Brazilian investment bank Icatu Friday denied it had been formally approached to run troubled Bamerindus, the country's fourth largest private bank, the private Invest News agency reported.

Invest News, quoting Icatu director Pedro Bodin in Rio de Janeiro, said Icatu had been approched informally by both the Central Bank and Bamerindus but only for advice on transfer of ownership operations.
"At no point have we been contacted by the Central Bank or by Bamerindus with a view to taking over the running of the bank," Bodin said.
Slightly contradictory newspapers reports Friday said a deal had been struck envisaging handing over the management of Bamerindus to either Icatu or investment bank Pactual.
Trade was suspended in Bamerindus shares, but resumed after Bamerindus denied Icatu had agreed to take over its management.
A Central Bank spokesman said he was unable to comment on the reports.
Invest News said Bodin had stressed his bank was an investment house and had no experience running banks.
